questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
As the given series is in G.P., so its sum is

$\dfrac{{\left(1 + x\right)}^{10}\left[1 - {\left(\dfrac{x}{1 + x}\right)}^{11}\right]}{\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{1 + x}\right)}$

Coefficient of $x^{7}$, is ${11}_{C7} = {11}_{C4} = 330$

${11}^{1011} = {\left({11}^{3}\right)}^{327} = {\left(9k + 8\right)}^{327}$

when divided by $9$ is equivalent to the division of

Now, ${\left(1011\right)}^{11} = {\left(9m + 3\right)}^{11}$

${3}^{11} = {\left(9\right)}^{5} \times 3$

i.e. remainder$= 0$

$∴ {11}^{1011} + {1011}^{11}$ has same remainder as $8$.

questions.q: $Cr n - 1 = \left(k^{2} - 8\right) Cr + 1 n$ if and only if :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $Cr n - 1 = \left(k^{2} - 8\right) Cr + 1 n . . . \left($i\right)$

$⇒ \mathop{r + 1 ≥ 0, r ≥ 0 ⏟}_{r ≥ 0}$

$⇒ $\dfrac{Cr n - 1}{Cr + 1 n} =$k^{2} - 8$

$⇒ $\dfrac{\dfrac{\left(n - 1\right) !}{r ! \left(n - r - 1\right) !}}{\dfrac{n !}{\left(r + 1\right) ! \left(n - r - 1\right) !}} =$k^{2} - 8$

$⇒ $\dfrac{r + 1}{n} =$k^{2} - 8$

$⇒ k^{2} - 8 > 0$

$⇒ ( k - $2\sqrt{2} ) ($k + $2\sqrt{2} )$> 0$

$⇒ k \in ( - $\infty , --2\sqrt{2} )∪ ( 2\sqrt{2}, \infty ) . . . (ii )$

Using equation \left($i\right)$,

$⇒ n ≥ r + 1$

$⇒ $\dfrac{r + 1}{n} \le$1$

$⇒ k^{2} - 8 ≤ 1$

$⇒ k^{2} - 9 ≤ 0$

$⇒ - 3 ≤ k ≤ 3 . . . ( ii )$

From equation \left($ii\right)\text{and}\left(iii\right)$ we get,

$k \in [ - 3, - 2\sqrt{2} )∪ ( 2\sqrt{2},3 ]

$

questions.q: If the number of integral terms in the expansion of \left(3\dfrac{1}{2} + 5\dfrac{1}{8}\right)n$ is exactly $33$, then the least value of $n$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(3\dfrac{1}{2} + 5\dfrac{1}{8}\right)n$

General term~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n \left(3\dfrac{1}{2}\right)n - r\left(5\dfrac{1}{8}\right)r$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n 3\dfrac{n - r}{2}5\dfrac{r}{8}$.

$\dfrac{n - r}{2}, \dfrac{r}{8}$~must be integer.

$\dfrac{n - r}{2} \in I ⇒ n - r = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 . . . . . . .$

$\dfrac{r}{8} \in I ⇒ r = 0, 8, 16, 24, 32 . . . .$

For rational term common powers$= 0, 8, 16, 24 . . . . . . .$

Number of integral term$= 33$

${T}_{s} = a + \left(s - 1\right)d ⇒ {T}_{33} = 0 + \left(33 - 1\right)8 = 256$.

Value of~$n = 256$.

We can cross check to verify answer.

$

questions.q: If the greatest value of the term independent of $x$~in the expansion of \left(xsin\alpha + a\dfrac{cos\alpha}{x}\right)10$ is $\dfrac{10 !}{\left(5 !\right)2},$~then the value of $a$ \text{ and } is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have, $r^{th}$~term in the expansion of~\left(xsin\alpha + a\dfrac{cos\alpha}{x}\right)10$~is

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 10 \left(xsin\alpha\right)10 - r\left(\dfrac{acos\alpha}{x}\right)r$

$r = 0, 1, 2, \ldots , 10$

${T}_{r + 1}$ will be independent of $x,$~when $10 - 2r = 0$

$⇒ r = 5$

Now,~${T}_{6} = C5 10 \left(xsin\alpha\right)5 \times \left(\dfrac{acos\alpha}{x}\right)5$

$= C5 10 \times a^{5} \times \dfrac{1}{25}\left(sin2\alpha\right)5$

${T}_{6}$~will be greatest, when $sin2\alpha = 1$

Therefore,~$C5 10 \dfrac{a5}{25} = C5 10$

$⇒ a = 2$

$

questions.q: Let the number $( 22{)}^{2022} + ( 2022{)}^{22}$ leave the remainder $\alpha$ when divided by $3$ and $\beta$ when divided by $7$. Then $( {α}^{2} + {β}^{2} )$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that& $\alpha$~be the remainder when~\left(22\right)2022 + \left(2022\right)22$~is divided by~$3$~and~$\beta$~be the remainder when the same is divided by~$7$.

$⇒ \left(22\right)2022 + \left(2022\right)22 = \left(21 + 1\right)2022 + \left(2022\right)22$.

Here~\left(2022\right)22$~is divisible by~$3$~as~$2022$~is divisible by~$3$.

So on expanding~\left(21 + 1\right)2022$, we get

$⇒ \left(21 + 1\right)2022 = C0 2022 \left(21\right)2022 + C1 2022 \left(21\right)2021 + . . . . . . + C2022 2022 \left(1\right)2022$

$= 3\left({3}^{2021} \times {7}^{2022} + C1 2022 \times {3}^{2020} \times {7}^{2021} + . . . . . .\right) + 1$

$= 3{k}_{1} + 1$

In this case the remainder is~$1$

Hence,~$\alpha = 1$

Now,~$⇒ \left(22\right)2022 + \left(2022\right)22 = \left(21 + 1\right)2022 + \left(2023 - 1\right)22$

Take~\left(2023 - 1\right)22$

$⇒ \left(2023 - 1\right)22 = C0 22 \left(2023\right)22 - C1 22 \left(2023\right)21 + . . . . . . + C22 22 \left(- 1\right)22$

$= 7\left(C0 22 \left(7\right)21\left(289\right)22 - C1 22 \left(7\right)20\left(289\right)21 + . . . . . .\right) + 1$

$= 7{k}_{2} + 1$

$⇒ \left(21 + 1\right)2022 + \left(2023 - 1\right)22 = 7{k}_{1} + 1 + 7{k}_{2} + 1$

$= 7\mu + 2$

$⇒ \beta = 2$.

Hence,~${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = {1}^{2} + {2}^{2} = 5$.

Therefore, the required answer is~$5$.

questions.q: If& $C3 2n : C3 n = 10: 1,$~then the ratio~  \left(n^{2} + 3n\right): \left(n^{2} - 3n + 4\right)$& is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have been given that& $C3 2n : C3 n = 10$

We know that~$Cr n = \dfrac{n !}{r ! \left(n - r\right) !}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(2n\right) !}{3 ! \left(2n - 3\right) !}}{\dfrac{n !}{3 ! \left(n - 3\right) !}} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n\right) !}{3 ! \left(2n - 3\right) !} \times \dfrac{3 ! \left(n - 3\right) !}{n !} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n\right)\left(2n - 1\right)\left(2n - 2\right)\left(2n - 3\right) !}{\left(2n - 3\right) !} \times \dfrac{\left(n - 3\right) !}{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right) !} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n\right)\left(2n - 1\right)\left(2n - 2\right)}{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)} = 10$

$⇒ \left(4\right)\left(2n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right) = 10$

$⇒ 8n - 4 = 10n - 20$

$⇒ n = 8$

Hence, the value of~$\dfrac{n^{2} + 3n}{n^{2} - 3n + 4}$~is~$= \dfrac{{8}^{2} + 3\left(8\right)}{{8}^{2} - 3\left(8\right) + 4} = \dfrac{88}{44} = 2$

Therefore, the value of~$\dfrac{n^{2} + 3n}{n^{2} - 3n + 4}$~is~$2: 1$.

questions.q: If some three consecutive coefficients in the binomial expansion of \left(x + 1\right)n$ in powers of $x$ are in the ratio $2: 15: 70,$ then the average of these three coefficients is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
From the given condition

${ }^{n}{C}_{r}{:}^{n}{C}_{r + 1}{:}^{n}{C}_{r + 2} = 2: 15: 70$

$⇒ \dfrac{{ }^{n}{C}_{r}}{{ }^{n}{C}_{r + 1}} = \dfrac{2}{15}$ and $\dfrac{{ }^{n}{C}_{r + 1}}{{ }^{n}{C}_{r + 2}} = \dfrac{15}{70}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r\right) ! \cdot r !}\right)\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}\right) = \dfrac{2}{15}$~and~\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}\right)\left(\dfrac{n !}{\left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 2\right) !}\right) = \dfrac{15}{70}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}{\left(n - r\right) ! \cdot r !} = \dfrac{2}{15}$~and~$\dfrac{\left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 2\right) !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !} = \dfrac{3}{14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) \cdot r !}{\left(n - r\right) \cdot \left(n - r - 1\right) ! \cdot r !} = \dfrac{2}{15}$~and~$\dfrac{\left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 2\right) \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !}{\left(n - r - 1\right) \cdot \left(n - r - 2\right) ! \cdot \left(r + 1\right) !} = \dfrac{3}{14}$

$⇒ \dfrac{r + 1}{n - r} = \dfrac{2}{15}$~and~$\dfrac{r + 2}{n - r - 1} = \dfrac{3}{14}$

$⇒ 17r = 2n - 15$ and $17r = 3n - 31$

$⇒ 3n - 31 = 2n - 15, ⇒ n = 16$ and $r = 1$

Hence, average $= \dfrac{{ }^{n}{C}_{r}{+}^{n}{C}_{r + 1}{+}^{n}{C}_{r + 2}}{3}$

$= \dfrac{{ }^{16}{C}_{1}{+}^{16}{C}_{2}{+}^{16}{C}_{3}}{3}$

$= 232 .$

$

questions.q:
Among the statements :

$( S1 ) : {2023}^{2022} - {1999}^{2022}$~is divisible by $8$.

$( S2 ) : 13 ( 13{)}^{n} - 11n - 13$~is divisible by $144$~for infinitely many~$n \in \mathbb{N}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$( S1 ) : ( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2022}$~is divisible by $8$

Now we know that $( x - y )$~divides~ \left(x^{n} - y^{n}\right) ∀ n \in \mathbb{N}$

So,~\left(2023 - 1999\right)$~divides~$( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2022}$

$⇒ 24$~divides~$( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2002}$

$⇒ 8$~will divide~$( 2023{)}^{2022} - ( 1999{)}^{2002}$

As~$8$~divides~$24$

Hence,~ \left(S1\right)$~is correct

Now solving,

\left(S2\right): 13\left(13\right)n - 11n - 13$~is divisible by~$144$~for~$n \in \mathbb{N}$

So using binomial theorem in~\left(1 + 12\right)n$~we get,

$13\left(1 + 12\right)n - 11n - 13$

$= 13\left({}^{n}{C}_{0}{+}^{n}{C}_{1}12{+}^{n}{C}_{2}{12}^{2} + . . . {+}^{n}{C}_{n}{12}^{n}\right) - 11n - 13$

$= 12 \times 13n - 11n + {12}^{2}\lambda$

$= 145n + 144\lambda$~which is~not divisible by~$144$

Hence,~ \left(S2\right)& is incorrect

$

questions.q: The remainder when \left(2023\right)2023$ is divided by $35$ is$

\left[as2030ismultipleof 35\right]$

$- {7}^{2023} = - \left({7}^{3}\right)674 \times7$

$= - \left({7}^{3}\right)674 \times7 = - \left(343\right)674 \times7$

$= - \left(343\right)674 \times7 = - \left(350 - 7\right)674 \times7$

$= \left(35{k}_{1} + {7}^{674}\right)\times\left(-7\right)$

So, again using binomial we get remainder as~$- 7 \times {7}^{674}$

Again rewriting the expression as~

Again using binomial we get remainder as~

Again using binomial we get remainder as~${7}^{25}$.

Now again rewriting~ \left({7}^{3}\right)$8 $\times$7 = \left($350 - 7\right)8 $\times$7$

Using binomial remainder will be~${7}^{9}$~which can be written as~ \left({7}^{3}\right)3 = \left(350 - 7\right)3$,

Let the coefficient of $x^{r}$ in the expansion of \left(x + 3\right)n - 1 + \left(x + 3\right)n - 2\left(x + 2\right) + \left(x + 3\right)n - 3\left(x + 2\right)2 + . ... + \left(x + 2\right)n - 1$ be ${α}_{r}$. If$\mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{n}{α}_{r} = {β}^{n} - {γ}^{n}, \beta, \gamma \in N$, then the value of ${β}^{2} + {γ}^{2}$ equals _______.

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let,

$S = \left(x + 3\right)n - 1 + \left(x + 3\right)n - 2\left(x + 2\right) + \left(x + 3\right)n - 3\left(x + 2\right)2 + . .... + \left(x + 2\right)n - 1$

Now, using the sum of G.P formula we get,

$⇒ S = \left(x + 3\right)n - 1 \left[\dfrac{1 - \left(\dfrac{x + 2}{x + 3}\right)n}{1 - \dfrac{x + 2}{x + 3}}\right]

$⇒ S = \left($x + 3\right)n - \left($x + 2\right)n$

Now, finding the sum of coefficients we get,

$⇒ ∑ {α}_{r} = ∑ \left($x + 3\right)n - ∑ \left($x + 2\right)n$

$⇒ {4}^{n} - {3}^{n} = {β}^{n} - {γ}^{n}\left$\${\text{by taking}x = 1\right\}

So, on comparing both side we get, \beta =$4, $\gamma =$3$

Hence, ${β}^{2} + {γ}^{2} = 16 + 9 = 25

We have to check& ${11}^{n} > {10}^{n} + {9}^{n}$

$⇒ {11}^{n} - {9}^{n} > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ ( 10 + 1{)}^{n} - ( 10 - 1{)}^{n} > {10}^{n}$

Using~\left(a + b\right)n - \left(a - b\right)n = 2\left[C1 n \cdot a^{n - 1} \cdot b + C3 n \cdot a^{n - 3} \cdot b^{3} + C5 n \cdot a^{n - 5} \cdot b^{5} + . . .\right]$

$⇒ 2\left[C1 n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} + C3 n \cdot {10}^{n - 3} + C5 n \cdot {10}^{n - 5} + ⋯ ⋯\right] > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ 2n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} + 2 \left[C3 n \cdot {10}^{n - 3} +C5 n \cdot {10}^{n - 5} +⋯ ⋯\right] > {10}^{n}$~$\ldots \left(1\right)$

For~$n = 5,$~the~$L . H . S .$~is~$2 \cdot5 \cdot {10}^{4} +2 \left[C3 5 \cdot {10}^{2} +C5 5\right]$

$⇒ {10}^{5} + 2\left[C3 5 \cdot {10}^{2} +C5 5\right] > {10}^{5}$~which is true.

Now, for~$n = 6, 7, 8, \ldots \ldots , 100$

$2n \cdot {10}^{n - 1}> {10}^{n}$

$⇒ 2n \cdot {10}^{n - 1} +$+2\left[C3 n \cdot {10}^{n - 3} +C5 n \cdot {10}^{n - 5} +⋯ ⋯\right] > {10}^{n}$

$⇒ {11}^{n} - {9}^{n} > {10}^{n}$~for all~$n = 5, 6, 7, \ldots \ldots , 100$

For $n = 4,$~the inequality \left(1\right)$~is not satisfied.

Hence, the inequality does not hold good for~$n = 1, 2, 3, 4$

So, required number of elements$= 96 .$
